data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 3 public peers (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private competitors including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method here. Using total raised ($280M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $476M. Peer-median analysis cannot be deployed: while 8 same-sector peers exist, none meet narrow filters for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient data density (threshold ≥3 datapoints). Constructing a median from all-sector peers would introduce unacceptable methodological bias given heterogeneity in quantum hardware approaches, funding timelines, and commercialization stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $405M to $547M, centered at $476M. Material uncertainties include the absence of a robust peer-median cross-check, which limits confidence in the step-up multiplier. The quantum computing sector remains pre-revenue or early-revenue dominant, making comparable company multiples unreliable. Path to liquidity and technical differentiation among hardware modalities (superconducting, trapped-ion, photonic) represent key value drivers not captured in this quantitative framework alone.
